title: Patch-Seq Recording and Extraction
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bepyjdpw
materials: 96 well microcentrifuge tube racks (3, at least 1 metal) (Thermo Fisher XTPCR96)
Patched cell containers (provided by molecular biology)
PF0285 DAB Detection of Biocytin Labeled Tissue
PF0289 Post Patch Clamp Slice Fixation
RP0235 Patch-Seq Internal Solution with Biocytin
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
NOTE: The equipment is sensitive to static charge. Be sure to touch the metal surface of the air table to ground yourself before touching any equipment.
Follow prompts for the custom workflow sequencing engine.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Slices
steps.instruction: Obtain tissue slices using SOP AF0099 (mouse) or SOP PF0295 (human).

substeps.instruction: Incubate mouse tissue in ACSF.IV solution for 1 to 5 hours after slicing.
Incubate human tissue in ACSF.VIII solution for at least 1 hour (can be indefinite).

steps.title: Rig Setup and Maintenance
steps.instruction: Perform morning maintenance, start up and clean the ephys rig and workstation, and sign into the Laboratory Information Management system.

substeps.instruction: Pull glass pipettes on a Narishige PC-10 puller to be used as electrodes (target resistance 3-7 MΩ).
Label patched cell containers with the date (YYMMDD) on the side and a three-digit tube number on the cap.

steps.title: Load and Image Slice
steps.instruction: Position the tissue slice in the chamber and capture initial images.

substeps.instruction: Load a slice into the chamber using a Pasteur pipette and center it on the stage using forceps.
Set the harp across the slice using forceps.
Switch to 40x objective, lower it until the white part is immersed in the bath, and use coarse focus to locate cells.
Follow the custom workflow sequencing engine prompts to collect 4x corner images of the slice.

steps.title: Select Target Cell
steps.instruction: Identify a healthy target cell below the cut surface of the slice.

substeps.instruction: Switch to 40x objective using the PatchPad Approach switch and set PatchPad to slow speed.
Manually lower the objective if necessary to bring tissue into focus.
Search for healthy-looking cells (plump, 3D, with contrast) and target Cre+ or Cre- cells based on the region of interest plan.
Once a cell is selected, switch back to the 4x objective.

steps.title: Prepare and Test Pipette
steps.instruction: Fill the electrode with internal solution and verify its resistance.

substeps.instruction: Fill the glass pipette tip with ~1 µl of internal solution using a fresh microloader tip on a 20 µl pipettor; flick/shake to remove bubbles.
Attach the pipette to the channel one headstage, slide it onto the silver wire, and tighten the holding screw a quarter turn past finger tight.
Apply 70 to 80 mbar of positive pressure by pushing the syringe and sealing the stopcock.
Move the pipette into the bath above the slice using the Control Cube.
Check the electrode resistance (Rss); it should be in the 3-7 MΩ range. Replace if outside this range.

steps.title: Approach and Seal Cell
steps.instruction: Position the pipette on the target cell and establish a GΩ seal.

substeps.instruction: Switch to 40x objective, set PatchPad and Control Cube to slow speed, and lower the objective and pipette to the tissue surface.
Visualize positive pressure on screen and check for clogs.
Focus on the target cell and collect a 40x image via the workflow engine.
Focus back to the pipette at the tissue surface, click 'Auto Cp Fast' to remove transients, and zero the resistance (lock symbol under Pipette Offset -> Auto). Collect the InBath sweep.
Lower the pipette to the target cell at an angle until it leaves a slight dimple in the cell surface.
Release positive pressure and apply negative pressure (suction) to seal. Apply holding potential to maintain the cell at -70 mV.
Verify a GΩ seal (Rss > 1000 MΩ) and collect the CellAttached sweep. If the seal fails to reach 1 GΩ, abort the attempt.

steps.title: Whole-Cell Break-In
steps.instruction: Break into the cell to achieve whole-cell configuration.

substeps.instruction: Apply quick pulses of negative pressure to break into the cell; use the 'Zap' function if the cell resists.
Once whole-cell configuration is achieved, collect the break-in sweep.
If access resistance is > 20 MΩ or break-in fails, abort the attempt.
Switch to 4x objective, focus on the pipette tip, and collect an image of the cell's location.
Collect 40x epifluorescence and bright field images of the cell.
Focus up to the slice surface and measure the cell's depth.
Switch to current clamp and run appropriate stimulus sets.
Monitor pipette placement and adjust for drift to keep it centered on the cell.
Record observations in the JSON form.

steps.title: Cell Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract the cellular contents after the recording period.

substeps.instruction: Switch back to voltage clamp and note the extraction start time in the JSON form.
Re-center the pipette and slowly apply negative pressure while monitoring the soma shape and membrane stability in the test pulse window.
If the membrane destabilizes, release pressure and wait for stabilization before retrying. If the seal is lost, move immediately to expulsion.

steps.title: Retraction and Expulsion
steps.instruction: Retract the pipette from the tissue and expel the contents into a storage tube.

substeps.instruction: Once the cell has visibly shrunk, slowly retract the pipette to obtain a nucleated patch.
Re-center the pipette, adjust and lock off the negative pressure.
Retract completely from tissue, switch to 4x objective, and use the 'H out' button to remove the pipette from the bath.
Insert the pipette into the expulsion device and apply ~0.1 ml of positive pressure to the syringe.
Insert the pipette tip into a numbered patched cell container containing S4 buffer, touching the bottom of the tube.
Allow contents to drain, then spin down the tube in a microcentrifuge for 5 seconds if bubbles are present.
Flash freeze the tube in a metal rack on dry ice.

steps.title: Data Finalization and Cleanup
steps.instruction: Complete the experimental documentation and shut down the rig.

substeps.instruction: Note the tube ID and expulsion outcome (bubbles, solution travel) in the JSON form.
Package and upload data to the Laboratory Information Management System.
If finished with the slice, fix it according to SOP PF0289 and note the histology well name.
Enter container IDs, Cre status, and structure into the LIMS under the specimen ID.
Perform evening maintenance: clean and shut down the ephys rig and perform room-level duties.

description: An overview of the process is detailed below – each of these steps is run through a custom workflow sequencing engine.
